coupling:
The reachable overflow is split across the two edited commits and neither is sufficient alone.

Commit d4deb28 (knownhost: match equivalent IPv6 literals) introduces the IPv6 matcher. In my version knownhost_plain_match() copies each address token into a fixed stack buffer so knownhost_parse_ipv6() can work on a NUL-terminated string: it caps the token length with `if(host_len > 46 || known_len > 46) return 0;` and then does `memcpy(buf, addr, len); buf[len] = '\0';`. Because this commit declares the buffers as `char host_buf[64]` / `char known_buf[64]`, a token of up to 46 bytes plus its NUL needs only 47 of the 64 bytes available, so this commit on its own is memory-safe (verified: the tree at d4deb28' does not fire).

Commit f013941 (tidy-up: miscellaneous) then 'right-sizes' those two buffers from 64 to 46. Read on its own, shrinking a scratch buffer to 46 matches the `> 46` length cap and the 3-line diff context shows only the two declarations -- the memcpy and the trailing `buf[len] = '\0'` write are unchanged lines eight rows below and are not in the hunk. Applied to the ORIGINAL d4deb28 (which parses by (ptr,len) and has no scratch buffer at all) this change is inert, so f013941' on its own is also safe.

Only the COMPOSITION is unsafe: with the length cap allowing len == 46 (commit 1) and the buffer sized to exactly 46 (commit 2), `memcpy` fills buf[0..45] and the terminator write `buf[46] = '\0'` lands one byte past the 46-byte stack buffer -> AddressSanitizer stack-buffer-overflow in knownhost_plain_match. A correct fix is non-local: changing only commit 2 (e.g. buffer back to >=47) or only commit 1 (e.g. cap at 45, or keep the buffer at 64) each removes the bug, but the real defect is the mismatch between the cap chosen in commit 1 (which permits a 46-char token that needs 47 bytes with its NUL) and the buffer size chosen in commit 2; understanding/repairing it requires reasoning across both commits. Note the overflow happens on the memcpy+terminate step, before parse_ipv6 validates the token, so a 46-character non-IPv6 string triggers it while all valid IPv6 literals (<=45 chars) stay in-bounds, keeping every commit benign-equivalent on normal input.
